questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: Kai, 16, wants to contribute to a Roth IRA. Which of his income counts as earned income for IRA purposes?

choices.text: $500 of birthday gifts from relatives
$2,400 in wages from a part-time job
$300 of interest from a savings account
A $1,000 weekly allowance from parents

questions.correct_answer: $2,400 in wages from a part-time job
questions.intro: To contribute to an IRA, you must have earned income (taxable compensation), such as wages, salaries, tips, or net self-employment earnings. Gifts, allowances, interest, and dividends do not count. There is no minimum age.
questions.feedback: Wages are earned income; gifts, allowance, and interest are not.
questions.topic: Roth IRA eligibility and contribution rules
sources: IRS (Publication 590-A and 590-B): IRA contributions require taxable compensation (earned income) and are limited to the lesser of the annual limit or compensation; Roth contributions are not deductible; qualified Roth distributions are tax-free. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/individual-retirement-arrangements-iras)

IRS (Retirement topics: IRA contribution limits): The IRA contribution limit and Roth income limits change by tax year; this course uses stated hypothetical amounts. (https://www.irs.gov/retirement-plans/plan-participant-employee/retirement-topics-ira-contribution-limits)

IRS (Publication 590-A): Excess IRA contributions are subject to a 6% excise tax for each year they remain in the account; contributions for a year can be made until the tax return due date (not including extensions). (https://www.irs.gov/publications/p590a)

questions.domain: Retirement Accounts: IRAs, Roth IRAs, 401(k)s, and 403(b)s
questions.prompt: For this scenario, assume the annual IRA contribution limit is $7,000. Kai earned $3,200 from his job this year. What is the most he can contribute to a Roth IRA for the year?
questions.intro: The most you can contribute to IRAs for a year is the LESSER of the annual limit or your earned income for that year.
questions.feedback: $3,200 is less than $7,000, so his limit is $3,200.

questions.prompt: Roth IRA eligibility also depends on income. For this scenario, assume single filers can contribute fully below $150,000 of modified income and not at all above $165,000. Leo's modified income is $172,000. Can he contribute directly to a Roth IRA?

choices.text: Yes, the full amount, because he has earned income
Yes, but only half the limit
Yes, if he contributes before January
No; his income is above the limit

questions.correct_answer: No; his income is above the limit
questions.intro: Roth IRAs have income limits: above a certain modified adjusted gross income (MAGI), direct Roth contributions are reduced or not allowed. The limits change each year. Traditional IRA contributions have no income cap, though deductibility can be limited.
questions.feedback: $172,000 is above the $165,000 upper limit in this scenario.

questions.feedback: Custodial Roth IRAs let minors with earned income save for retirement.
